The only project-specific file of the kit. Skills and agents read it first. The shared engineering rules loaded from the parent `.claude/rules/` folder also apply: `RULES.md` R1–R11 and the code standards of `be-development-rules.md` and `fe-development-rules.md`.

## Stack

- Nx 18.1.2 monorepo with explicit targets in each `project.json`, pnpm, TypeScript 5.9, Jest 29.

- Database: TypeORM 0.3.22 on Postgres 15. `synchronize` is off; schema changes are migrations in `libs/backend-common`.
- Frontend: `apps/web`, Next 15.5 Pages Router (`src/pages`, no App Router, no Server Components), React 18.2, MUI 5 with Emotion, `react-hook-form` with `yup`, axios through the API client in `src/services`, Jest with Testing Library.

## Source of truth

- `libs/contract` (`@roombook/contract`) is the source of truth for routes, message patterns, queue names, DTO classes, error codes and job payloads. Use what it exports. Do not invent a route, pattern, field or error code.
- Errors cross service boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`, with `errorCode` taken from `ErrorCodeEnum`.

## Architecture

- Controllers are thin: at most five statements, all delegating to a service. No logic in controllers.
- Every POST, PUT and PATCH handler takes a DTO class with class-validator decorators as its body.
- Services hold business rules and delegate data access to repositories.
- Database transactions live in repositories only, never in services.
- The gateway holds no database access and no business rules; it validates input and forwards over NATS.
- Every controller, service and provider is registered in exactly one module.
- No literal ports, hosts, URLs or secrets in source files; configuration comes from environment variables read through the config module.
- Every deployable service has a health endpoint: a health message pattern on each NATS service, exposed by the gateway as `GET /api/health/<service>`.

## TypeScript

- Never use `interface`; use `class` for DTOs and `type` for everything else.
- Never use `any`.
- Never use an inline object type as a function parameter; define a named DTO class.
- Every repository method has an explicit return type.
- Named imports only; no `import * as`.

## Files and style

- File names are kebab-case and describe their purpose.
- Keep every code file under 200 lines; split by concern.
- No comments that restate what the code does. A comment is allowed only for a non-obvious constraint, one short line.

## Conventions

- Backend feature folder: `<feature>.module.ts`, `.controller.ts`, `.service.ts`, `.repository.ts`, each with a `*.spec.ts` next to it. Repositories are `@Injectable` classes that inject `Repository<Entity>` and `DataSource`.
- Domain code throws through the exception helper in `@roombook/backend-common`; never return an error as a normal payload.

- Queues: `BullModule.registerQueue({ name: QueueEnum.X })`, producers with `@InjectQueue`, processors extending `WorkerHost`.
- Web: a file under `src/pages/<feature>/` is the route; its components live in `src/views/<feature>/`; one function per endpoint in `src/services/<entity>.service.ts`; per-path MUI imports; specs mock the service layer, not axios; branch on `errorCode`, never on message text. Never import `@roombook/backend-common` in the web app.

## Tests

- Every new or modified service has at least one unit test in a `*.spec.ts` file next to it.
- Write the failing test before the implementation.
- A change is finished only when `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` all pass.

1	# prevent-overlapping-room-bookings: Bookings of the same room may no longer overlap
2	
3	Tier: change
4	Why this tier: it adds a conflict rule to the existing `bookings` capability; create, update, idempotency and the page already exist.
5	
6	## Why
7	Two bookings can occupy the same room at the same time (archived assumption "overlapping bookings of one room are allowed"). Create and update now answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` instead, also under concurrency.
8	Sample values, all on 2030-01-07 UTC: rooms R1 and R2; A = a stored booking of R1 09:00–10:00; K1 = an unused idempotency key. Every error body is `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`.
9	
10	## Requirements
11	### ADDED bookings
12	#### BKG-012: Overlap rule
13	The system SHALL treat two bookings as overlapping only when they have the same `roomId` and each starts before the other ends (half-open spans, compared as instants).
14	- Scenario: inside or across. WHEN a span of R1 is 09:30–10:30, 08:00–09:00:00.001, 09:15–09:45 or 08:00–11:00 THEN it overlaps A
15	- Scenario: touching. WHEN a span of R1 is 10:00–11:00 or 08:00–09:00 THEN it does not overlap A
16	- Scenario: other room. WHEN a span of R2 is 09:00–10:00 THEN it does not overlap A
17	#### BKG-013: Create rejects an overlap
18	The system SHALL answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` on `POST /api/bookings` when the new span overlaps (BKG-012) a stored booking, storing no booking and enqueueing no confirmation job.
19	- Scenario: rejected. WHEN R1 09:30–10:30 is posted with K1 THEN 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, only A exists in R1 and the queue got no job
20	- Scenario: allowed. WHEN R1 10:00–11:00 is posted, or R2 09:00–10:00 THEN 201
21	- Scenario: replay is not a conflict. WHEN the request that created A is posted again with its key THEN the IDM-003 replay answers 201, not 409
22	#### BKG-014: Update rejects an overlap
23	The system SHALL answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` on `PATCH /api/bookings/:id` when the merged span overlaps (BKG-012) another booking, leaving the booking unchanged; a booking never conflicts with itself.
24	- Scenario: rejected. WHEN B of R1 10:00–11:00 is patched with `{ "startsAt": "2030-01-07T09:59:59.999Z" }` THEN 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and B still starts at 10:00
25	- Scenario: itself. WHEN A is patched with `{ "title": "Retro" }`, or with `{ "endsAt": "2030-01-07T09:30:00Z" }` THEN 200
26	- Scenario: touching. WHEN B is patched with `{ "endsAt": "2030-01-07T12:00:00Z" }`, or A with `{ "startsAt": "2030-01-07T08:00:00Z" }` THEN 200
27	#### BKG-015: Span writes of one room are serialised
28	The system SHALL run the overlap check and the write of a create or a span-changing update inside one transaction that holds a lock on the room, so that concurrent writes cannot both pass the check.
29	- Scenario: simultaneous creates. WHEN R2 09:00–10:00 and R2 09:30–10:30 are posted at the same moment with different keys against the real database THEN exactly one answers 201, the other 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, and one booking exists in R2
30	- Scenario: simultaneous updates. WHEN A (09:00–10:00) is patched with `endsAt` 10:45 and C of R1 (11:00–12:00) with `startsAt` 10:15 at the same moment THEN exactly one answers 200 and the other 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`
31	#### BKG-016: The database refuses an overlap
32	The system SHALL back BKG-012 with an exclusion constraint `EXCL_bookings_room_span` on `bookings` and map its violation to 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`.
33	- Scenario: direct write. WHEN a row of R1 09:30–10:30 is inserted directly next to A THEN Postgres rejects it with `EXCL_bookings_room_span`; WHEN the row is R1 10:00–11:00 THEN it is stored
34	### MODIFIED booking-idempotency
35	#### IDM-007: Failed requests do not consume the key
36	The system SHALL store nothing against a key whose request is answered 400, 404, 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` or 503 before the transaction commits.
37	- Scenario: key reusable. WHEN K1 is posted with `endsAt` equal to `startsAt` (400), then with an unknown room (404), then with B1 THEN the third answers 201 without `Idempotency-Replayed`
38	- Scenario: overlap is not stored. WHEN R1 09:30–10:30 is posted with K1 (409), A is deleted and the same request is posted with K1 again THEN 201 without `Idempotency-Replayed`
39	### MODIFIED bookings-page
40	#### BPG-005: Create form
41	The system SHALL offer a form with room, title, organizer email, start and end (entered as UTC), validate it before sending, and refetch the list after a 201.
42	- Scenario: submit. WHEN the form holds R1, "Sprint planning", `ann@example.com`, `2030-01-07T09:00`, `2030-01-07T10:00` and is submitted THEN `createBooking` receives B1 and a UUID key, the form resets and the list is fetched again
43	- Scenario: client validation. WHEN the title is empty, the email is `x`, or end is not later than start THEN the field shows an error and `createBooking` is not called
44	- Scenario: API error. WHEN `createBooking` rejects with 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` "Room … was not found" THEN an alert shows that message and the entered values stay
45	- Scenario: overlap. WHEN `createBooking` rejects with 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` "The room is already booked in that time span" THEN an alert in the form shows that message, all five values stay, and the next submit carries a new key (BPG-006)
46	#### BPG-007: Edit a row
47	The system SHALL let the user edit title, start and end of a row and send only the fields whose value changed.
48	- Scenario: title only. WHEN a booking starting `2030-01-07T09:00:30.123Z` has its title changed to "Retro" and is saved THEN `updateBooking` receives exactly `{ title: "Retro" }` and the list is fetched again
49	- Scenario: no change. WHEN the dialog is saved untouched THEN `updateBooking` is not called
50	- Scenario: invalid. WHEN end is not later than start THEN the field shows the BPG-005 error; WHEN the API answers 400 THEN its message is shown in the dialog
51	- Scenario: overlap. WHEN `updateBooking` rejects with 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` THEN the dialog stays open, shows the API's message and keeps the entered title, start and end
52	
53	## Design
54	- Guard: inside the existing create and update transactions, `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('room:' || roomId, 0))`, then the overlap query, then the write. The lock waits (unlike the key try-lock), so the loser sees the winner's row and gets the friendly 409.
55	- The exclusion constraint alone is not the guard: two concurrent conflicting inserts can deadlock on it. It is the backstop (BKG-016); behind the room lock it never races.
56	- Constraint: `EXCLUDE USING gist ("room_id" WITH =, tstzrange("starts_at", "ends_at") WITH &&)`, default `[)` bounds, in a new migration that first runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist`, and as `@Exclusion` on the entity. Assumption: the migration role may create that extension (trusted contrib in Postgres 15); it is not a package dependency.
57	- Create order: key try-lock → stored key (replay or reuse) → room lock → overlap check → insert booking and key. The key is read first, so a replay never meets its own booking. The service order stays validation → room lookup → transaction → enqueue, so 400 and 404 win over 409.
58	- Update: the booking row lock first (BKG-009), then the room lock and the check against the merged span excluding its own `id`, only when `startsAt` or `endsAt` changes. A title-only patch takes no room lock and runs no check.
59	- Lock order is always key or row before room, and nothing takes a room lock first, so no cycle.
60	- The overlap is thrown inside the transaction through `ExceptionHelper.conflict`; the rollback leaves no key row (IDM-007) and the service never reaches the enqueue. `BookingService` needs no code change; its specs gain the cases.
61	- The overlap query uses the ORM (`LessThan`, `MoreThan`, `Not`); raw SQL only for the advisory lock and the migration.
62	- Assumption: the message is "The room is already booked in that time span"; the web app shows it as received and branches on nothing.
63	- Assumption: the web forms already show `error.message` and keep their values for any `ApiError`; the frontend tasks prove it and change code only if a spec fails. `use-idempotency-key.ts` already treats this 409 as a final answer.
64	- Existing specs that store several bookings in one room and span (integration specs, fixtures) move to distinct rooms or spans; their assertions stay.
65	- Home of each rule: overlap predicate, room lock and the 409 → `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.ts`, called by `idempotent-booking.repository.ts` and `booking.repository.ts`; constraint name → `booking.entity.ts`; constraint → 409 mapping → the shared rethrow in `booking.repository.ts`.
66	
67	## Risks
68	| Risk | Applies | Note | Task |
69	|---|---|---|---|
70	| R-01 | no | no new input field | - |
71	| R-02 | yes | the check must use the merged span read under the row lock and other rows read under the room lock | T06 |
72	| R-03 | no | no new side effect; a rejected create enqueues nothing (BKG-013) | - |
73	| R-04 | no | no new parsing; spans arrive as parsed instants | - |
74	| R-05 | no | no new validator or parser | - |
75	| R-06 | no | compares `Date` instants and a `uuid` column, not raw strings | - |
76	| R-07 | no | no new rows, keys or jobs | - |
77	| R-08 | yes | overlap invariant; BKG-016 | T02 |
78	| R-09 | yes | room lock, exclusion constraint and rollback on the real database | T06 |
79	| R-10 | yes | "does not conflict with itself" and "no job enqueued" assertions name BKG-014 and BKG-013 | T07 |
80	| R-11 | yes | one overlap rule for create and update | T03 |
81	| R-12 | yes | raw SQL only for the advisory lock; overlap query through the ORM | T03 |
82	| R-13 | no | no new column, field or option | - |
83	| R-14 | no | key lifecycle unchanged; this 409 is a final answer under BPG-006, asserted in T09 | - |
84	| R-15 | no | no list mutation changes | - |
85	| R-16 | no | no list or select changes | - |
86	| R-17 | no | edit still sends only changed fields; a rejection sends nothing new | - |
87	
88	## Tasks
89	- [ ] T01 @main [BKG-013] Add `BOOKING_OVERLAP = 'CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP'` to `ErrorCodeEnum` before the tracks start; the contract spec asserts the value | libs/contract/src/lib/error-code.enum.ts, libs/contract/src/lib/contract.constants.spec.ts
90	- [ ] T02 @be [BKG-016, R-08] Migration with `btree_gist` and `EXCL_bookings_room_span`, `@Exclusion` and the exported constraint name on the entity; integration spec inserts an overlapping row directly and expects Postgres to refuse, and a touching row to be stored | libs/backend-common/src/lib/database/migrations/1731400000000-add-bookings-overlap-exclusion.ts, libs/backend-common/src/lib/database/migrations/index.ts, libs/backend-common/src/lib/entities/booking.entity.ts, libs/backend-common/src/index.ts, libs/backend-common/src/lib/database/booking-overlap-constraint.int.spec.ts
91	- [ ] T03 @be [BKG-012, R-11, R-12] `requireFreeSpan(manager, span)`: room lock, ORM overlap query excluding an optional own id, 409 through `ExceptionHelper`; unit spec asserts the lock statement, the query conditions and the 409 for a create-shaped and an update-shaped call | apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.ts, apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.spec.ts

# prevent-overlapping-room-bookings: Bookings of the same room may no longer overlap

Tier: change
Why this tier: it adds a conflict rule to the existing `bookings` capability; create, update, idempotency and the page already exist.

## Why
Two bookings can occupy the same room at the same time (archived assumption "overlapping bookings of one room are allowed"). Create and update now answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` instead, also under concurrency.
Sample values, all on 2030-01-07 UTC: rooms R1 and R2; A = a stored booking of R1 09:00–10:00; K1 = an unused idempotency key. Every error body is `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`.

## Requirements
### ADDED bookings
#### BKG-012: Overlap rule
The system SHALL treat two bookings as overlapping only when they have the same `roomId` and each starts before the other ends (half-open spans, compared as instants).
- Scenario: inside or across. WHEN a span of R1 is 09:30–10:30, 08:00–09:00:00.001, 09:15–09:45 or 08:00–11:00 THEN it overlaps A
- Scenario: touching. WHEN a span of R1 is 10:00–11:00 or 08:00–09:00 THEN it does not overlap A
- Scenario: other room. WHEN a span of R2 is 09:00–10:00 THEN it does not overlap A
#### BKG-013: Create rejects an overlap
The system SHALL answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` on `POST /api/bookings` when the new span overlaps (BKG-012) a stored booking, storing no booking and enqueueing no confirmation job.
- Scenario: rejected. WHEN R1 09:30–10:30 is posted with K1 THEN 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, only A exists in R1 and the queue got no job
- Scenario: allowed. WHEN R1 10:00–11:00 is posted, or R2 09:00–10:00 THEN 201
- Scenario: replay is not a conflict. WHEN the request that created A is posted again with its key THEN the IDM-003 replay answers 201, not 409
#### BKG-014: Update rejects an overlap
The system SHALL answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` on `PATCH /api/bookings/:id` when the merged span overlaps (BKG-012) another booking, leaving the booking unchanged; a booking never conflicts with itself.
- Scenario: rejected. WHEN B of R1 10:00–11:00 is patched with `{ "startsAt": "2030-01-07T09:59:59.999Z" }` THEN 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and B still starts at 10:00
- Scenario: itself. WHEN A is patched with `{ "title": "Retro" }`, or with `{ "endsAt": "2030-01-07T09:30:00Z" }` THEN 200
- Scenario: touching. WHEN B is patched with `{ "endsAt": "2030-01-07T12:00:00Z" }`, or A with `{ "startsAt": "2030-01-07T08:00:00Z" }` THEN 200
#### BKG-015: Span writes of one room are serialised
The system SHALL run the overlap check and the write of a create or a span-changing update inside one transaction that holds a lock on the room, so that concurrent writes cannot both pass the check.
- Scenario: simultaneous creates. WHEN R2 09:00–10:00 and R2 09:30–10:30 are posted at the same moment with different keys against the real database THEN exactly one answers 201, the other 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, and one booking exists in R2
- Scenario: simultaneous updates. WHEN A (09:00–10:00) is patched with `endsAt` 10:45 and C of R1 (11:00–12:00) with `startsAt` 10:15 at the same moment THEN exactly one answers 200 and the other 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`
#### BKG-016: The database refuses an overlap
The system SHALL back BKG-012 with an exclusion constraint `EXCL_bookings_room_span` on `bookings` and map its violation to 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`.
- Scenario: direct write. WHEN a row of R1 09:30–10:30 is inserted directly next to A THEN Postgres rejects it with `EXCL_bookings_room_span`; WHEN the row is R1 10:00–11:00 THEN it is stored
### MODIFIED booking-idempotency
#### IDM-007: Failed requests do not consume the key
The system SHALL store nothing against a key whose request is answered 400, 404, 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` or 503 before the transaction commits.
- Scenario: key reusable. WHEN K1 is posted with `endsAt` equal to `startsAt` (400), then with an unknown room (404), then with B1 THEN the third answers 201 without `Idempotency-Replayed`
- Scenario: overlap is not stored. WHEN R1 09:30–10:30 is posted with K1 (409), A is deleted and the same request is posted with K1 again THEN 201 without `Idempotency-Replayed`
### MODIFIED bookings-page
#### BPG-005: Create form
The system SHALL offer a form with room, title, organizer email, start and end (entered as UTC), validate it before sending, and refetch the list after a 201.
- Scenario: submit. WHEN the form holds R1, "Sprint planning", `ann@example.com`, `2030-01-07T09:00`, `2030-01-07T10:00` and is submitted THEN `createBooking` receives B1 and a UUID key, the form resets and the list is fetched again
- Scenario: client validation. WHEN the title is empty, the email is `x`, or end is not later than start THEN the field shows an error and `createBooking` is not called
- Scenario: API error. WHEN `createBooking` rejects with 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` "Room … was not found" THEN an alert shows that message and the entered values stay
- Scenario: overlap. WHEN `createBooking` rejects with 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` "The room is already booked in that time span" THEN an alert in the form shows that message, all five values stay, and the next submit carries a new key (BPG-006)
#### BPG-007: Edit a row
The system SHALL let the user edit title, start and end of a row and send only the fields whose value changed.
- Scenario: title only. WHEN a booking starting `2030-01-07T09:00:30.123Z` has its title changed to "Retro" and is saved THEN `updateBooking` receives exactly `{ title: "Retro" }` and the list is fetched again
- Scenario: no change. WHEN the dialog is saved untouched THEN `updateBooking` is not called
- Scenario: invalid. WHEN end is not later than start THEN the field shows the BPG-005 error; WHEN the API answers 400 THEN its message is shown in the dialog
- Scenario: overlap. WHEN `updateBooking` rejects with 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` THEN the dialog stays open, shows the API's message and keeps the entered title, start and end

## Design
- Guard: inside the existing create and update transactions, `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('room:' || roomId, 0))`, then the overlap query, then the write. The lock waits (unlike the key try-lock), so the loser sees the winner's row and gets the friendly 409.
- The exclusion constraint alone is not the guard: two concurrent conflicting inserts can deadlock on it. It is the backstop (BKG-016); behind the room lock it never races.
- Constraint: `EXCLUDE USING gist ("room_id" WITH =, tstzrange("starts_at", "ends_at") WITH &&)`, default `[)` bounds, in a new migration that first runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist`, and as `@Exclusion` on the entity. Assumption: the migration role may create that extension (trusted contrib in Postgres 15); it is not a package dependency.
- Create order: key try-lock → stored key (replay or reuse) → room lock → overlap check → insert booking and key. The key is read first, so a replay never meets its own booking. The service order stays validation → room lookup → transaction → enqueue, so 400 and 404 win over 409.
- Update: the booking row lock first (BKG-009), then the room lock and the check against the merged span excluding its own `id`, only when `startsAt` or `endsAt` changes. A title-only patch takes no room lock and runs no check.
- Lock order is always key or row before room, and nothing takes a room lock first, so no cycle.
- The overlap is thrown inside the transaction through `ExceptionHelper.conflict`; the rollback leaves no key row (IDM-007) and the service never reaches the enqueue. `BookingService` needs no code change; its specs gain the cases.
- The overlap query uses the ORM (`LessThan`, `MoreThan`, `Not`); raw SQL only for the advisory lock and the migration.
- Assumption: the message is "The room is already booked in that time span"; the web app shows it as received and branches on nothing.
- Assumption: the web forms already show `error.message` and keep their values for any `ApiError`; the frontend tasks prove it and change code only if a spec fails. `use-idempotency-key.ts` already treats this 409 as a final answer.
- Existing specs that store several bookings in one room and span (integration specs, fixtures) move to distinct rooms or spans; their assertions stay.
- Home of each rule: overlap predicate, room lock and the 409 → `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.ts`, called by `idempotent-booking.repository.ts` and `booking.repository.ts`; constraint name → `booking.entity.ts`; constraint → 409 mapping → the shared rethrow in `booking.repository.ts`.

## Risks

|---|---|---|---|

1	# Project rules: roombook
2	
3	The only project-specific file of the kit. Skills and agents read it first. The shared engineering rules loaded from the parent `.claude/rules/` folder also apply: `RULES.md` R1–R11 and the code standards of `be-development-rules.md` and `fe-development-rules.md`.
4	
5	## Stack
6	
7	- Nx 18.1.2 monorepo with explicit targets in each `project.json`, pnpm, TypeScript 5.9, Jest 29.
8	- Backend: NestJS 11.0.20. `apps/gateway` (HTTP under `/api`), `apps/booking` and `apps/room` (NATS request/reply through `@nestjs/microservices`, one queue group per service, no JetStream), `apps/worker` (BullMQ 5.79.1 through `@nestjs/bullmq` on Redis 7), `libs/backend-common` (config, entities, migrations, errors, NATS client).
9	- Database: TypeORM 0.3.22 on Postgres 15. `synchronize` is off; schema changes are migrations in `libs/backend-common`.
10	- Frontend: `apps/web`, Next 15.5 Pages Router (`src/pages`, no App Router, no Server Components), React 18.2, MUI 5 with Emotion, `react-hook-form` with `yup`, axios through the API client in `src/services`, Jest with Testing Library.
11	- Validation: class-validator 0.14 and class-transformer for DTOs; Joi for config.
12	
13	## Source of truth
14	
15	- `libs/contract` (`@roombook/contract`) is the source of truth for routes, message patterns, queue names, DTO classes, error codes and job payloads. Use what it exports. Do not invent a route, pattern, field or error code.
16	- Errors cross service boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`, with `errorCode` taken from `ErrorCodeEnum`.
17	
18	## Architecture
19	
20	- Controllers are thin: at most five statements, all delegating to a service. No logic in controllers.
21	- Every POST, PUT and PATCH handler takes a DTO class with class-validator decorators as its body.
22	- Services hold business rules and delegate data access to repositories.
23	- Database transactions live in repositories only, never in services.
24	- The gateway holds no database access and no business rules; it validates input and forwards over NATS.
25	- Every controller, service and provider is registered in exactly one module.
26	- No literal ports, hosts, URLs or secrets in source files; configuration comes from environment variables read through the config module.
27	- Every deployable service has a health endpoint: a health message pattern on each NATS service, exposed by the gateway as `GET /api/health/<service>`.
28	
29	## TypeScript
30	
31	- Never use `interface`; use `class` for DTOs and `type` for everything else.
32	- Never use `any`.
33	- Never use an inline object type as a function parameter; define a named DTO class.
34	- Every repository method has an explicit return type.
35	- Named imports only; no `import * as`.
36	
37	## Files and style
38	
39	- File names are kebab-case and describe their purpose.
40	- Keep every code file under 200 lines; split by concern.
41	- No comments that restate what the code does. A comment is allowed only for a non-obvious constraint, one short line.
42	
43	## Conventions
44	
45	- Backend feature folder: `<feature>.module.ts`, `.controller.ts`, `.service.ts`, `.repository.ts`, each with a `*.spec.ts` next to it. Repositories are `@Injectable` classes that inject `Repository<Entity>` and `DataSource`.
46	- Domain code throws through the exception helper in `@roombook/backend-common`; never return an error as a normal payload.
47	- Entities and migrations live in `libs/backend-common`: explicit snake_case names, uuid primary keys, `timestamp with time zone`.
48	- Queues: `BullModule.registerQueue({ name: QueueEnum.X })`, producers with `@InjectQueue`, processors extending `WorkerHost`.
49	- Web: a file under `src/pages/<feature>/` is the route; its components live in `src/views/<feature>/`; one function per endpoint in `src/services/<entity>.service.ts`; per-path MUI imports; specs mock the service layer, not axios; branch on `errorCode`, never on message text. Never import `@roombook/backend-common` in the web app.
50	
51	## Tests
52	
53	- Every new or modified service has at least one unit test in a `*.spec.ts` file next to it.
54	- Write the failing test before the implementation.
55	- A change is finished only when `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` all pass.
56	- Integration specs against the real database are named `*.int.spec.ts`, so the build excludes them like any spec. Each one skips itself when the database is not configured, which keeps the unit run green without the stack: `const describeWithDatabase = process.env.DB_HOST ? describe : describe.skip;`. They use the exported `dataSource` of `@roombook/backend-common` (or a `DataSource` built from `process.env`), run the real repository code, and delete the rows they create. Run them with the Integration command below: it loads the configuration into the process, so you never read the file.
57	
58	## Commands
59	
60	Shell is for these commands only, one per call. Anything else is denied and wastes a turn.
61	
62	| Purpose | Command |
63	|---|---|
64	| Kit | `node cr/bin/cr.mjs validate [<id>]`, `node cr/bin/cr.mjs tick <id> <T..>`, `node cr/bin/cr.mjs archive <id>` |
65	| One project | `pnpm nx lint <project>`, `pnpm nx test <project>`, `pnpm nx build <project>` |
66	| Everything | `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run test` |
67	| One spec file | `npx jest -c <project>/jest.config.ts <path>` |
68	| Integration specs | `scripts/stack-up.sh` once, then `node --env-file=.env node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js -c <project>/jest.config.ts --testMatch "**/*.int.spec.ts" --runInBand` |
69	| Types | `npx tsc --noEmit -p <project>/tsconfig.app.json` |
70	| Git, read-only | `git status`, `git diff`, `git log` |
71	| Listing | `ls <path>` |
72	
73	`curl`, `cd`, pipes, `&&`, `;`, loops, redirects, heredocs, `sed`, `perl` and `python` are not available. Read with Read, Grep and Glob; change files with Edit and Write.
74	
75	## Safety
76	
77	- Never read `.env` or `.env.*` files; refer to configuration by variable name.
78	- Git is local only: no remote, no push, no pull request. Commit only when told to.
79	- Do not add dependencies.
80

1	# Risk catalogue
2	
3	Bug classes that shipped in earlier work. Every feature and change lists each ID once in its `## Risks` table: `yes` with the task that tests it, or `no` with the reason. Side: `be` backend, `fe` frontend.
4	
5	## R-01 Explicit null on an optional input (be)
6	- Ask: which optional fields can arrive as `null`, and what do the parser and the `??` or `COALESCE` fallback do with it?
7	- Rule: optional means absent. Reject `null` at the DTO, or handle it as a named case.
8	- Test: send `null` for every optional field; assert rejection or the stated result. Cover both sides of every fallback.
9	
10	## R-02 Read-modify-write outside the guard (be)
11	- Ask: is any value read before the lock or transaction and written back inside it?
12	- Rule: read, merge and write inside the same transaction that takes the lock.
13	- Test: two partial updates of different fields on one record; both survive.
14	
15	## R-03 Side effect after commit with no recovery (be)
16	- Ask: what happens if the queue, bus or mail call fails, hangs, or the process dies after commit?
17	- Rule: give the call a timeout, never swallow its failure silently, and state the recovery path (outbox, sweep or replay). A consumer must be safe to run twice.
18	- Test: make the side effect fail and hang; assert the recorded state and the retry path.
19	
20	## R-04 Date-time without an offset (be)
21	- Ask: how is `2030-01-07T09:00` read, and does the answer depend on the server's time zone?
22	- Rule: reject offset-less input or define it as UTC, in one helper used everywhere.
23	- Test: the same input under two `TZ` values gives the same instant.
24	
25	## R-05 Validator and parser disagree (be)
26	- Ask: does the validator accept any form the parser reads differently?
27	- Rule: validate and parse with the same strict grammar.
28	- Test: unusual but valid forms (ordinal or week dates, extra precision, other case) are rejected or parsed to the right value.
29	
30	## R-06 Equality on non-normalised input (be)
31	- Ask: is a hash, fingerprint or uniqueness check computed on raw strings?
32	- Rule: parse and normalise before hashing or comparing.
33	- Test: two spellings of the same value are treated as equal.
34	
35	## R-07 Unbounded growth (be)
36	- Ask: which rows, keys or jobs are written and never removed?
37	- Rule: give each a TTL or retention setting, or record the decision to keep it in Design.
38	- Test: assert the retention setting.
39	
40	## R-08 Invariant only in application code (be)
41	- Ask: does the invariant still hold if one write path forgets the check or the lock?
42	- Rule: back it with a database constraint (unique, check, exclusion). Keep the application check for the friendly error and map the constraint error to the same answer.
43	- Test: write a violating row directly; the database refuses.
44	
45	## R-09 Guarantee tested only against mocks (be)
46	- Ask: is a lock, transaction, constraint or raw SQL statement covered only by specs that mock the database?
47	- Rule: one integration spec against the real database for each such guarantee.
48	- Test: concurrent requests against the real database; exactly one wins.
49	
50	## R-10 A test that locks in a bug (be)
51	- Ask: does any spec assert that an error is swallowed, ignored or that data is dropped?
52	- Rule: assert the behaviour a requirement states, never the current accident.
53	- Test: each "does not throw" or "is ignored" assertion names its requirement ID.
54	
55	## R-11 One rule, two homes (be, fe)
56	- Ask: is the same rule implemented in two layers, two paths (create and update) or two forms?
57	- Rule: one function or schema per rule, called from every path.
58	- Test: the rule's spec exercises it through each caller.
59	
60	## R-12 Hand-kept copy of the schema (be)
61	- Ask: is there a column list, row mapper or transaction scaffold written by hand where the ORM provides it?
62	- Rule: use the ORM API; raw SQL only where the ORM cannot express the statement, and then never with a hand-kept column list.
63	- Test: none; reviewed in the diff.
64	
65	## R-13 Dead data (be)
66	- Ask: is any new column, field or option written and never read?
67	- Rule: do not add it.
68	- Test: none; a reader exists for every new column.
69	
70	## R-14 Client retry identity (fe)
71	- Ask: when a request times out or returns 5xx or "in progress", does the retry carry the same idempotency key?
72	- Rule: keep the key until the user changes the payload; drop it only after a final answer.
73	- Test: a 503 then a retry sends the same key; an edit then a submit sends a new one.
74	
75	## R-15 List state after a mutation (fe)
76	- Ask: after deleting the last row of the last page, where is the user?
77	- Rule: refetch after every mutation and step back to the last non-empty page.
78	- Test: delete the only row on page N; page N-1 shows.
79	
80	## R-16 Hardcoded fetch cap (fe)
81	- Ask: does a list or a select silently stop at a literal limit?
82	- Rule: page through, or show that the list is cut.
83	- Test: more items than the cap; all are reachable or the cut is visible.
84	
85	## R-17 Precision lost on a round trip (fe)
86	- Ask: does editing one field rewrite another through a lossy format?
87	- Rule: send only the fields the user changed; never reformat a value the user did not touch.
88	- Test: edit one field of a record whose other values carry full precision; they are unchanged.

1	# prevent-overlapping-room-bookings: Bookings of the same room may no longer overlap
2	
3	Tier: change
4	Why this tier: it adds a conflict rule to the existing `bookings` capability; create, update, idempotency and the page already exist.
5	
6	## Why
7	Two bookings can occupy the same room at the same time (archived assumption "overlapping bookings of one room are allowed"). Create and update now answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` instead, also under concurrency.
8	Sample values, all on 2030-01-07 UTC: rooms R1 and R2; A = a stored booking of R1 09:00–10:00; K1 = an unused idempotency key. Every error body is `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`.
9	
10	## Requirements
11	### ADDED bookings
12	#### BKG-012: Overlap rule
13	The system SHALL treat two bookings as overlapping only when they have the same `roomId` and each starts before the other ends (half-open spans, compared as instants).
14	- Scenario: inside or across. WHEN a span of R1 is 09:30–10:30, 08:00–09:00:00.001, 09:15–09:45 or 08:00–11:00 THEN it overlaps A
15	- Scenario: touching. WHEN a span of R1 is 10:00–11:00 or 08:00–09:00 THEN it does not overlap A
16	- Scenario: other room. WHEN a span of R2 is 09:00–10:00 THEN it does not overlap A
17	#### BKG-013: Create rejects an overlap
18	The system SHALL answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` on `POST /api/bookings` when the new span overlaps (BKG-012) a stored booking, storing no booking and enqueueing no confirmation job.
19	- Scenario: rejected. WHEN R1 09:30–10:30 is posted with K1 THEN 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, only A exists in R1 and the queue got no job
20	- Scenario: allowed. WHEN R1 10:00–11:00 is posted, or R2 09:00–10:00 THEN 201
21	- Scenario: replay is not a conflict. WHEN the request that created A is posted again with its key THEN the IDM-003 replay answers 201, not 409
22	#### BKG-014: Update rejects an overlap
23	The system SHALL answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` on `PATCH /api/bookings/:id` when the merged span overlaps (BKG-012) another booking, leaving the booking unchanged; a booking never conflicts with itself.
24	- Scenario: rejected. WHEN B of R1 10:00–11:00 is patched with `{ "startsAt": "2030-01-07T09:59:59.999Z" }` THEN 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and B still starts at 10:00
25	- Scenario: itself. WHEN A is patched with `{ "title": "Retro" }`, or with `{ "endsAt": "2030-01-07T09:30:00Z" }` THEN 200
26	- Scenario: touching. WHEN B is patched with `{ "endsAt": "2030-01-07T12:00:00Z" }`, or A with `{ "startsAt": "2030-01-07T08:00:00Z" }` THEN 200
27	#### BKG-015: Span writes of one room are serialised
28	The system SHALL run the overlap check and the write of a create or a span-changing update inside one transaction that holds a lock on the room, so that concurrent writes cannot both pass the check.
29	- Scenario: simultaneous creates. WHEN R2 09:00–10:00 and R2 09:30–10:30 are posted at the same moment with different keys against the real database THEN exactly one answers 201, the other 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, and one booking exists in R2

33	- Scenario: direct write. WHEN a row of R1 09:30–10:30 is inserted directly next to A THEN Postgres rejects it with `EXCL_bookings_room_span`; WHEN the row is R1 10:00–11:00 THEN it is stored

54	- Guard: inside the existing create and update transactions, `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('room:' || roomId, 0))`, then the overlap query, then the write. The lock waits (unlike the key try-lock), so the loser sees the winner's row and gets the friendly 409.
55	- The exclusion constraint alone is not the guard: two concurrent conflicting inserts can deadlock on it. It is the backstop (BKG-016); behind the room lock it never races.

Assumption: the migration role may create that extension (trusted contrib in Postgres 15); it is not a package dependency.

16	- Ask: what happens if the queue, bus or mail call fails, hangs, or the process dies after commit?

1	# prevent-overlapping-room-bookings: Bookings of the same room may no longer overlap
2	
3	Tier: change
4	Why this tier: it adds a conflict rule to the existing `bookings` capability; create, update, idempotency and the page already exist.
5	
6	## Why
7	Two bookings can occupy the same room at the same time (archived assumption "overlapping bookings of one room are allowed"). Create and update now answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` instead, also under concurrency.
8	Sample values, all on 2030-01-07 UTC: rooms R1 and R2; A = a stored booking of R1 09:00–10:00; K1 = an unused idempotency key. Every error body is `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }`.
9	
10	## Requirements
11	### ADDED bookings
12	#### BKG-012: Overlap rule
13	The system SHALL treat two bookings as overlapping only when they have the same `roomId` and each starts before the other ends (half-open spans, compared as instants).
14	- Scenario: inside or across. WHEN a span of R1 is 09:30–10:30, 08:00–09:00:00.001, 09:15–09:45 or 08:00–11:00 THEN it overlaps A
15	- Scenario: touching. WHEN a span of R1 is 10:00–11:00 or 08:00–09:00 THEN it does not overlap A
16	- Scenario: other room. WHEN a span of R2 is 09:00–10:00 THEN it does not overlap A
17	#### BKG-013: Create rejects an overlap
18	The system SHALL answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` on `POST /api/bookings` when the new span overlaps (BKG-012) a stored booking, storing no booking and enqueueing no confirmation job.
19	- Scenario: rejected. WHEN R1 09:30–10:30 is posted with K1 THEN 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, only A exists in R1 and the queue got no job
20	- Scenario: allowed. WHEN R1 10:00–11:00 is posted, or R2 09:00–10:00 THEN 201
21	- Scenario: replay is not a conflict. WHEN the request that created A is posted again with its key THEN the IDM-003 replay answers 201, not 409
22	#### BKG-014: Update rejects an overlap
23	The system SHALL answer 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` on `PATCH /api/bookings/:id` when the merged span overlaps (BKG-012) another booking, leaving the booking unchanged; a booking never conflicts with itself.
24	- Scenario: rejected. WHEN B of R1 10:00–11:00 is patched with `{ "startsAt": "2030-01-07T09:59:59.999Z" }` THEN 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` and B still starts at 10:00
25	- Scenario: itself. WHEN A is patched with `{ "title": "Retro" }`, or with `{ "endsAt": "2030-01-07T09:30:00Z" }` THEN 200
26	- Scenario: touching. WHEN B is patched with `{ "endsAt": "2030-01-07T12:00:00Z" }`, or A with `{ "startsAt": "2030-01-07T08:00:00Z" }` THEN 200
27	#### BKG-015: Span writes of one room are serialised
28	The system SHALL run the overlap check and the write of a create or a span-changing update inside one transaction that holds a lock on the room, so that concurrent writes cannot both pass the check.
29	- Scenario: simultaneous creates. WHEN R2 09:00–10:00 and R2 09:30–10:30 are posted at the same moment with different keys against the real database THEN exactly one answers 201, the other 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`, and one booking exists in R2
30	- Scenario: simultaneous updates. WHEN A (09:00–10:00) is patched with `endsAt` 10:45 and C of R1 (11:00–12:00) with `startsAt` 10:15 at the same moment THEN exactly one answers 200 and the other 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`
31	#### BKG-016: The database refuses an overlap
32	The system SHALL back BKG-012 with an exclusion constraint `EXCL_bookings_room_span` on `bookings` and map its violation to 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP`.
33	- Scenario: direct write. WHEN a row of R1 09:30–10:30 is inserted directly next to A THEN Postgres rejects it with `EXCL_bookings_room_span`; WHEN the row is R1 10:00–11:00 THEN it is stored
34	### MODIFIED booking-idempotency
35	#### IDM-007: Failed requests do not consume the key
36	The system SHALL store nothing against a key whose request is answered 400, 404, 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` or 503 before the transaction commits.
37	- Scenario: key reusable. WHEN K1 is posted with `endsAt` equal to `startsAt` (400), then with an unknown room (404), then with B1 THEN the third answers 201 without `Idempotency-Replayed`
38	- Scenario: overlap is not stored. WHEN R1 09:30–10:30 is posted with K1 (409), A is deleted and the same request is posted with K1 again THEN 201 without `Idempotency-Replayed`
39	### MODIFIED bookings-page
40	#### BPG-005: Create form
41	The system SHALL offer a form with room, title, organizer email, start and end (entered as UTC), validate it before sending, and refetch the list after a 201.
42	- Scenario: submit. WHEN the form holds R1, "Sprint planning", `ann@example.com`, `2030-01-07T09:00`, `2030-01-07T10:00` and is submitted THEN `createBooking` receives B1 and a UUID key, the form resets and the list is fetched again
43	- Scenario: client validation. WHEN the title is empty, the email is `x`, or end is not later than start THEN the field shows an error and `createBooking` is not called
44	- Scenario: API error. WHEN `createBooking` rejects with 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` "Room … was not found" THEN an alert shows that message and the entered values stay
45	- Scenario: overlap. WHEN `createBooking` rejects with 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` "The room is already booked in that time span" THEN an alert in the form shows that message, all five values stay, and the next submit carries a new key (BPG-006)
46	#### BPG-007: Edit a row
47	The system SHALL let the user edit title, start and end of a row and send only the fields whose value changed.
48	- Scenario: title only. WHEN a booking starting `2030-01-07T09:00:30.123Z` has its title changed to "Retro" and is saved THEN `updateBooking` receives exactly `{ title: "Retro" }` and the list is fetched again
49	- Scenario: no change. WHEN the dialog is saved untouched THEN `updateBooking` is not called
50	- Scenario: invalid. WHEN end is not later than start THEN the field shows the BPG-005 error; WHEN the API answers 400 THEN its message is shown in the dialog
51	- Scenario: overlap. WHEN `updateBooking` rejects with 409 `CONFLICT.BOOKING_OVERLAP` THEN the dialog stays open, shows the API's message and keeps the entered title, start and end
52	
53	## Design
54	- Guard: inside the existing create and update transactions, `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('room:' || roomId, 0))`, then the overlap query, then the write. The lock waits (unlike the key try-lock), so the loser sees the winner's row and gets the friendly 409.
55	- The exclusion constraint alone is not the guard: two concurrent conflicting inserts can deadlock on it. It is the backstop (BKG-016); behind the room lock it never races.
56	- Constraint: `EXCLUDE USING gist ("room_id" WITH =, tstzrange("starts_at", "ends_at") WITH &&)`, default `[)` bounds, in a new migration that first runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist`, and as `@Exclusion` on the entity. Assumption: the migration role may create that extension (trusted contrib in Postgres 15); it is not a package dependency.
57	- Create order: key try-lock → stored key (replay or reuse) → room lock → overlap check → insert booking and key. The key is read first, so a replay never meets its own booking. The service order stays validation → room lookup → transaction → enqueue, so 400 and 404 win over 409.
58	- Update: the booking row lock first (BKG-009), then the room lock and the check against the merged span excluding its own `id`, only when `startsAt` or `endsAt` changes. A title-only patch takes no room lock and runs no check.
59	- Lock order is always key or row before room, and nothing takes a room lock first, so no cycle.
60	- The overlap is thrown inside the transaction through `ExceptionHelper.conflict`; the rollback leaves no key row (IDM-007) and the service never reaches the enqueue. `BookingService` needs no code change; its specs gain the cases.
61	- The overlap query uses the ORM (`LessThan`, `MoreThan`, `Not`); raw SQL only for the advisory lock and the migration.
62	- Assumption: the message is "The room is already booked in that time span"; the web app shows it as received and branches on nothing.
63	- Assumption: the web forms already show `error.message` and keep their values for any `ApiError`; the frontend tasks prove it and change code only if a spec fails. `use-idempotency-key.ts` already treats this 409 as a final answer.
64	- Existing specs that store several bookings in one room and span (integration specs, fixtures) move to distinct rooms or spans; their assertions stay.
65	- Home of each rule: overlap predicate, room lock and the 409 → `apps/booking/src/booking/booking-overlap.ts`, called by `idempotent-booking.repository.ts` and `booking.repository.ts`; constraint name → `booking.entity.ts`; constraint → 409 mapping → the shared rethrow in `booking.repository.ts`.
66
